tip: 떠나서 (tteonaseo) folds 'because' into the verb with -서 (-seo) – the reason comes first, the feeling last: friend-leaves-so, I'm-sad. English runs the opposite way.
친구가 부러워요 (chinguga bureowoyo) marks the friend with 가 (ga) as the subject – 부럽다 (bureopda) works like 'is enviable', so the envied person is the subject, not an object.
긴장돼요 (ginjangdwaeyo) is built on 되다 (doeda = become) – nerves are something that happens to you in Korean, not something you are.
있으면 (isseumyeon): the -(으)면 (-(eu)myeon) ending means both 'if' and 'when' – here it's 'whenever I'm alone at night', with no separate word for either.
부모님 (bumonim) take 계신 (gyesin) – 계시다 (gyesida) is the respect version of 있다 (itda = to be/stay): for parents and elders, even 'being' somewhere gets the polite verb.
놀랐어요 (nollasseoyo) needs no 'was' – 놀라다 (nollada) already means 'get startled', so Korean skips the passive English uses in 'I was startled'.
사람에게 (saramege): you're disappointed 'to' someone in Korean – 에게 (ege) marks the person who let you down, where English reaches for 'by' or 'in'.
눈물이 날 만큼 (nunmuri nal mankeum) = 'to the extent tears come out' – 만큼 (mankeum) follows a whole clause and turns it into 'enough to', measure before the feeling.
올 것 같아요 (ol geot gatayo): the -ㄹ (-l) on 올 marks a guess about the future – rain that hasn't come yet. A guess about the past switches to -ㄴ/은 (-n/eun).
한국 사람인 것 같아요 (hanguk saramin geot gatayo): a noun needs 인 (in) as the link before the guess – without it, 사람 (saram) can't connect to 'seems to be'.
그래요? (geuraeyo) turns into a question by rising tone alone – the statement uses the exact same words. Korean never flips word order to ask.
춥네요 (chumneyo) – the -네요 (-neyo) ending adds 'I just noticed': you felt the cold right now. Plain 추워요 (chuwoyo) would state a bare fact.
제 (je) is the humble 'my'. With friends you'd say 내 생각 (nae saenggak); 제 생각에는 (je saenggageneun) keeps the opinion polite from the very first word.
의견에 (uigyeone): 반대 (bandae = opposition) takes the particle 에 (e) – you object 'to' the opinion. Agreeing with 찬성 (chanseong) uses the same 에.
